facts.text: I can use the /show command with a unique Job ID to move a job to another server or channel, revive a lost job, or refresh an old job to make new variations, upscale, or use newer parameters and features.
The /show command only works for my own jobs.
Midjourney Job IDs are unique identifiers used for each image generated by Midjourney.
Midjourney Job IDs look like 9333dcd0-681e-4840-a29c-801e502ae424.
I can find a Midjourney Job ID in the first part of all image filenames.
I can find a Midjourney Job ID in the URLs on the Midjourney website.
I can find a Midjourney Job ID in an image's filename.
In the Midjourney web app, I can copy a Job ID from my member gallery by selecting ... > Copy... > Job ID.
In the Midjourney web app, the Job ID is the last part of the URL when viewing an image in my Midjourney gallery.
In the Midjourney web app, the Job ID is the last part of the file name when viewing an image I downloaded from my gallery.
I can use the /show command in any Bot Channel to revive a Job.
The /blend command allows uploading 2–5 images quickly to merge them into a novel new image.
The /blend command is the same as using multiple image prompts with /imagine, but the interface is optimized for easy use on mobile devices.
The /blend command works with up to 5 images.
The /blend command does not work with text prompts.
To use text and image prompts together, I should use image prompts and text with /imagine.
After typing /blend, I am prompted to upload two photos.
On mobile, I can drag and drop images from my hard drive or add images from my photo library when using /blend.
To add more images in /blend, I can select the optional/options field and select image3, image4, or image5.
The /blend command may take longer to start than other commands because images must be uploaded before the Midjourney Bot can process the request.
Blended images have a default 1:1 aspect ratio.
With /blend, I can select a square aspect ratio (1:1), portrait aspect ratio (2:3), or landscape aspect ratio (3:2) using the optional dimensions field.
Custom suffixes are added to the end of /blend prompts like any other /imagine prompt.
Aspect ratios specified as part of the /blend command override aspect ratios within a custom suffix.
For the best results with /blend, I should upload images that are the same aspect ratio as my desired result.
